decisions.decision: How should inference run on production cameras?
decisions.context: Cameras inspect defects on production lines, often without network access. Inference must remain available locally.

alternatives.label: Model as module in modular monolith
pros: Network independence: runs with the application
Tight budget: avoids separate service infrastructure
cons: Weekly updates: coordinate model and application releases

alternatives.label: Model as a service
pros: Separation: model can be managed independently
cons: Network independence: service may require connectivity
Tight budget: adds service operations

alternatives.label: Model in monolith
pros: Network independence: embed model in application
cons: Weekly updates: model changes are coupled to application code

chosen.label: Model as module in modular monolith

decisions.rationale: Network independence decides the choice: package inference with the camera application while keeping a module boundary. This gives up independent model service deployment.
consequences: Bundle model runtime and application for each device.
Model updates require a coordinated device release.

decisions.context: Inspection must continue when a camera has no network access. Predictions need to reach the local production application in real time.

alternatives.label: Local service/API based model serving
pros: Network independence: serves predictions locally
Low latency: avoids remote inference round trips
cons: Tight budget: adds local service/API operations

alternatives.label: Microservice based model serving
pros: Separation: model serving is distributed
cons: Network independence: remote calls can fail offline
Low latency: network adds delay

alternatives.label: Data batch based model serving
pros: Tight budget: scheduled batch processing
cons: Low latency: results are not immediate

decisions.rationale: Network independence decides the choice, with low latency also favoring local inference. The trade-off is operating a local serving interface on each device.
consequences: The camera application calls a device-local endpoint.
Local service health and resource use need operational attention.

decisions.context: The team retrains from newly labelled images every week. The workspace describes scheduled triggers and batch-based learning as alternatives for pipeline execution and training.

alternatives.label: On-schedule trigger with batch-based learning
pros: Weekly retraining: scheduled runs match the cadence
Tight budget: trains only on the weekly schedule
cons: Freshness: labels arriving just after a run wait until the next run

alternatives.label: On availability of new training data trigger with batch-based learning
pros: Freshness: starts when new data is available
cons: Tight budget: irregular runs may use more resources

alternatives.label: On-demand trigger with incremental learning
pros: Control: operators decide when to run
cons: Weekly retraining: depends on manual or external triggering

decisions.rationale: The stated weekly cadence decides the choice: scheduled batch training keeps execution predictable and bounded. It gives up immediate use of labels added between runs.
consequences: A failed run delays the next model unless operators rerun it.

decisions.decision: How should training data be versioned?
decisions.context: Newly labelled images feed recurring model training. Reproducing a model requires identifying which data version produced it.

alternatives.label: Data version repository
pros: Reproducibility: records specific data versions
cons: Tight budget: adds repository setup and maintenance

alternatives.label: Data versioning in code repository
pros: Tight budget: keeps versioning near existing code
cons: Reproducibility: large image datasets may be awkward to manage

alternatives.label: No data versioning
pros: Tight budget: no added versioning system
cons: Reproducibility: training inputs cannot be reliably restored

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice because weekly retraining must be traceable to its labelled images. It costs the small team additional repository operations.
consequences: Record the data version alongside each trained model.
Maintain the repository as part of the training workflow.

decisions.decision: How should model delivery be automated?
decisions.context: Models are retrained weekly and pushed to cameras that may be disconnected. A small team and tight infrastructure budget favor repeatable automation without a large platform.

alternatives.label: CI/CD pipeline
pros: Weekly delivery: automates repeatable build and deployment steps
cons: Network independence: device delivery still needs an offline-capable mechanism
Tight budget: pipeline maintenance has a cost

alternatives.label: Build and Deployment scripts
pros: Tight budget: straightforward automation
cons: Weekly delivery: manual execution can become error-prone

alternatives.label: Machine learning orchestrator
pros: Weekly delivery: coordinates multiple pipelines and components
cons: Tight budget: adds platform complexity

decisions.rationale: Weekly delivery decides the choice: CI/CD makes repeated model packaging and release steps consistent. The trade-off is pipeline upkeep, while delivery to disconnected cameras remains a separate design problem.
consequences: Automate model build and release validation.
The pipeline does not itself define how disconnected devices receive updates.

decisions.decision: How should production model versions be managed?
decisions.context: New models are delivered weekly to production devices. Defect detection needs a recovery path if a new release performs poorly.

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
pros: Reliable production: supports recovery to a prior model
cons: Tight budget: requires retaining and distributing prior artifacts

alternatives.label: N versions in production
pros: Reliable production: supports concurrent model versions
cons: Tight budget: more storage and release coordination

alternatives.label: Single model in production
pros: Tight budget: simplest active model state
cons: Reliable production: no explicit prior-version recovery path

decisions.rationale: Reliable production decides the choice: retaining a previous model enables recovery after a bad weekly release. This costs artifact storage and device delivery capacity.
consequences: Keep a known prior model artifact available for each device.

decisions.decision: What should be monitored in production?
decisions.context: Models operate on cameras that may be offline, so central observation cannot be assumed. Monitoring should still help detect quality problems and diagnose releases.

alternatives.label: Model performance monitoring
pros: Reliable production: tracks model quality measures
cons: Network independence: offline devices may delay reporting

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
pros: Diagnosis: captures inputs and outputs
cons: Tight budget: storage and review costs can grow

alternatives.label: No in-production monitoring
pros: Tight budget: avoids monitoring infrastructure
cons: Reliable production: quality regressions may go unnoticed

decisions.rationale: Reliable production decides the choice: observe model performance to identify regressions after releases. This gives up immediate centralized visibility when devices are disconnected.
consequences: Collect performance signals locally and report them when connectivity returns.
Choose domain-specific quality measures, which the design space does not specify.

uncovered: Offline device update protocol, including package transfer, retries, and fleet rollout strategy.
Camera hardware sizing, inference latency targets, and resource limits.
Model acceptance thresholds, defect class metrics, and labeling quality controls.
Security, authentication, and integrity checks for model artifacts and device updates.
Retention and privacy rules for production images, predictions, and logs.
